title: Notes Sql Constraints Primary Key And Foreign Key

items.question: Q1. What is the CHECK constraint, and why can a data type alone not replace it?
items.answer: Answer: Ans: A CHECK constraint applies a condition to a column, and a value is inserted only if the condition is true. If the condition is false, the database does not allow the value to be inserted. For example, an employee table can require that employee_age is greater than 18. Under labour law a person below 18 should not be hired, but an INT column accepts 17 as readily as 27. Without a CHECK constraint a record of an under-age person would be stored, and the company could face legal trouble over such data.

items.question: Q2. How do mandatory and optional fields of a registration form relate to constraints?
items.answer: Answer: Ans: In a form, the fields marked with an asterisk (*) are mandatory, such as first name, email id, phone number, job title and organisation. The form cannot be submitted until they are filled. Fields without the asterisk, such as location, are optional and can be left empty. In a table, a mandatory field corresponds to a column with the NOT NULL constraint, and an optional field corresponds to a column without it.

items.question: Q3. What problem does an optional field create, and how does DEFAULT solve it?
items.answer: Answer: Ans: When a field is optional, many users leave it empty, and the column stays empty for those records. For example, if marital status is optional, the organisation cannot tell whether such a person is married or single. The DEFAULT constraint solves this. It stores a fallback value, for example 'Single', whenever the user gives no value, so every record carries a value. This is a choice made on the requirement, because the field is not mandatory but a value is still wanted.

items.question: Q4. What is the DEFAULT constraint, and what kind of value can it hold?
items.answer: Answer: Ans: DEFAULT specifies the value that is stored automatically in a column when no value is supplied for it. The default can be of any data type, according to the column. A text column such as marital status can have the default 'Single', and a numeric column can have a number as its default. The value depends on the column and on the requirement.

items.question: Q5. On what basis is a column chosen as the primary key?
items.answer: Answer: Ans: A column is chosen as the primary key when its values can uniquely identify and describe the other data of each row. When a value of the column is known, it must be possible to find all the other values of that record. The column must also never contain NULL, because every row needs a value there. In practice this is an id column such as employee_id for an employee, product_id for a product or customer_id for a customer, since every such entity has an id. Q6. Why is an id column preferred over a name or an email column as the primary key? Explain with an example. Ans: Consider an employee table with the following rows. employee_id | employee_name | employee_email 101 | Amish | amish@gmail.com 102 | Amish | amish.k@gmail.com 103 | Rahul | NULL Sample Input: the three rows above Sample Output: The email id of the employee with id 101 is amish@gmail.com, and this answer is always exactly one row. The email id of the employee named Amish has two answers, so the name cannot identify a row; two people can share a name. The name of the employee whose email id is NULL cannot be found, so the email cannot identify every row; not every employee has an email id. Only employee_id identifies every row exactly once, so it is chosen as the primary key.

items.question: Q7. Can a column such as employee_email be made the primary key?
items.answer: Answer: Ans: Technically yes, but only when the data satisfies the rules. Every employee must have an email id, so the column never holds NULL, and all email ids must be different. If either condition fails, for example when some employees have no email id, the column cannot be the primary key. Since this cannot be guaranteed, an id column is chosen in almost every real table, and other columns such as email are made UNIQUE instead.

items.question: Q8. Can a table have more than one primary key?
items.answer: Answer: Ans: No. A table has only one primary key. Having two primary keys in one table is not possible.

items.question: Q9. What is a composite key?
items.answer: Answer: Ans: When two columns together satisfy the conditions of a primary key, they can be combined into a single key called a composite key. For example, employee_id and employee_email can be combined if both are unique and never NULL. The result is counted as one key made of two columns, and it is called a composite key, not two primary keys. In an interview, the answer to "can a table have two primary keys?" is that it cannot, but two columns can be combined into a composite key.

items.question: Q10. What is the difference between a PRIMARY KEY and a UNIQUE constraint?
items.answer: Answer: Ans: A primary key is UNIQUE plus NOT NULL, so its column can never hold NULL and each value identifies one row. A table can have only one primary key. A UNIQUE constraint only prevents duplicate values; it does not on its own demand a value in every row, and a table can contain it on more than one column. For example, employee_id is the primary key of an employee table, and employee_email is UNIQUE.

items.question: Q11. What kind of data belongs in a table?
items.answer: Answer: Ans: A table holds only the data that belongs to the entity it is named after. An employee table holds employee data such as the id, name, email id, age and marital status. It does not hold data that belongs to something else, such as the details of a department. Data of another entity is stored in its own table.

items.question: Q12. What is a foreign key?
items.answer: Answer: Ans: A foreign key is a column of one table that refers to the primary key of another table. It establishes a relationship between the two tables, so that additional information stored in the other table can be reached from the first.

items.question: Q13. What are parent and child tables?
items.answer: Answer: Ans: The table that holds the primary key being referred to is the parent table, and the table that holds the foreign key is the child table. The foreign key column in the child table does not really belong to the child's own data; it comes from outside, from the parent table. For example, a department table is the parent and an employee table that has a department_id column is the child. Q14. Why is a foreign key needed? Explain with an example. Ans: An employee table can answer questions about employees only. Suppose the data is as follows. employee table: employee_id | employee_name | department_id 101 | Amish | 3 department table: department_id | department_name | department_location 3 | Operations | C Block Sample Input: the two tables above Sample Output: To know where the employee 101 works, the department_id 3 is looked up in the department table. That row shows that the employee works in the Operations department located in C Block. The employee table alone cannot give this information, because it holds no department details. The department_id column connects the two tables, and that column is the foreign key.

items.question: Q15. Which column of the other table can a foreign key refer to?
items.answer: Answer: Ans: The foreign key refers to the primary key of the other table. In the example above, department_id is the primary key of the department table and the foreign key of the employee table. The column that is referred to is always the primary key of the parent table, and it is that link which establishes the relationship between the two tables.

items.question: Q16. A company keeps sales in a separate table. How is it linked with the employee table?
items.answer: Answer: Ans: The sales table has an employee_id column that is a foreign key referring to the employee_id primary key of the employee table. To find how much sales an employee has made, the rows of the sales table having that employee's id are read. Without the link, there would be no way to relate a sale to an employee.

items.question: Q17. In which order must two related tables be created?
items.answer: Answer: Ans: The parent table must be created first. The foreign key in the child table refers to a column of the parent, so the parent table has to exist already. For example, the department table is created first and then the employee table with its department_id foreign key. If the department_id column is just an ordinary column with no foreign key, the order does not matter, because there is no relationship to establish.

items.question: Q18. In which order must the data be inserted into related tables?
items.answer: Answer: Ans: The data of the parent table must be inserted first. A foreign key value in the child table can refer only to a primary key value that already exists in the parent table. An attempt to insert an employee with department id 4 fails if the department table has no department 4, because there is nothing to refer to. The department is inserted first, and then the employee.

items.question: Q19. Can a table have more than one foreign key?
items.answer: Answer: Ans: Yes. A table can have several foreign keys, each establishing a relationship with a different parent table. It can have only one primary key, but any number of foreign keys.
